title: Motifs et théorie de Hodge : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed page of a Bourbaki 'Tribu' (n° 59), the internal congress report. It carries the editorial comments of the congress on a draft (état) of the chapter 'Systèmes de racines', §9 'Classification des systèmes de racines'. This material became Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. VI (1968). It was most likely reused as scrap paper, or simply filed, among Grothendieck's motive notes. The neighbouring pages are handwritten notes on fibre functors and comparison isomorphisms for motives over fields isomorphic to C, so the archive's page 25 is an interleaved Bourbaki sheet.

The mathematics referred to is the standard classification of positive-definite Coxeter graphs, i.e. finite reflection groups over R.
- n°1 asks to state that one works over R, to index the vertices by a set I with ℓ elements, and to move Prop. 1 up.
- It notes that it is 'antibourbachique' for lemmas to have corollaries, so the corollaries on pp. 179 ff. are to be renamed lemmas.
- It asks for a clearer account of the edge-contraction procedure. Take an edge (i,j) of order 3 and replace the vertices i, j by a single new vertex p. Keep the old edges not meeting i or j, and join p to k whenever (i,k) or (j,k) was an edge, preserving orders. Algebraically, this substitutes a single variable ξ_p for ξ_i and ξ_j in the quadratic form, which stays positive definite.
- The lemma at the top of p. 181 then reads: a connected positive Coxeter graph either has exactly one branch point and all edges of order 3, or is a chain with at most one edge of order ≥4.
- Lemmas 3 and 4 are judged contrived ('canulés' or 'tirés par les cheveux'); the report asks to revert to état 3 (rédaction n° 383).
- n°2 is to open by saying that three exceptional families ('ces trois zèbres', evidently H3, H4 and I2(p) with p=5 or p≥7) correspond to groups (finite Coxeter groups). They cannot come from root systems because of the orders 5 or p≥7 (crystallographic restriction). All the other diagrams do come from root systems.
errors: No mathematical errors: the stated dichotomy (one branch point with all edges of order 3, or a chain with at most one edge of order ≥4) is the correct standard lemma in the classification of positive-definite Coxeter graphs, given that the graph is a tree with at most one branch point.

ideas.what: Contraction of an order-3 edge of a Coxeter graph preserves positivity of the associated quadratic form (substituting ξ_p for ξ_i and ξ_j).
ideas.modern_name: Edge-contraction lemma in the classification of finite Coxeter groups / Dynkin diagrams
ideas.usually_credited_to: Coxeter (1934), Witt; standard in Bourbaki Lie ch. VI §4 and Humphreys
ideas.where_published: Bourbaki, Groupes et algèbres de Lie, ch. IV–VI (1968), ch. VI §4

ideas.what: A connected positive Coxeter graph is either branched once with all edges of order 3, or a chain with at most one edge of order ≥4.
ideas.modern_name: Structure lemma for positive-definite Coxeter graphs

ideas.what: H3, H4 and I2(p) (p=5 or p≥7) are Coxeter groups but not Weyl groups of root systems.

missed.claim: Archival: a Bourbaki Tribu n° 59 sheet (editorial report on the root-systems chapter) is interleaved in Grothendieck's cote 18 motive notes, probably as reused paper. It is of minor interest for dating the folder and for the history of Bourbaki's Lie ch. VI (it mentions état 3 = rédaction n° 383). There is no new mathematics.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only for cataloguing and dating: it shows the page is not Grothendieck's own text and should not be read as part of the motives argument.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed Bourbaki editorial report on the standard classification of root systems and Coxeter graphs. It contains nothing original and is not by Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: '6tèmes' is Bourbaki shorthand ('six-tèmes') for 'systèmes'; the transcription correctly keeps the original.
'y peuvent pas' is colloquial for 'ils ne peuvent pas', as on the original.
The handwritten '25' at the bottom left is the archive page number and is missing from the transcription.
